files.lesson.md: --- order: 8 unit: shapes node: AC9M7SP02 n2 uses: [AC9M7M04 n2] # co-interior angles at parallel lines title: The quadrilateral family summary: "Quadrilaterals are named by their properties: parallel sides, equal sides and right angles. A shape that has all of another's properties belongs to it too: every square is a rectangle and a rhombus, and every rectangle is a parallelogram." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Is a square a rectangle? People argue about it. Maths settles it by asking what each name promises." connection: parallelogram-linkage app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8282 url: http://127.0.0.1:8282/index.html readySelector: "#gclass" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: shape.yml#explain-pic, caption: "A square: four equal sides (ticks), two pairs of parallel sides (arrows) and four right angles. So it is also a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram, a trapezium and a kite." } explainClip: query: { code: "@shape.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Named by properties" say: "A quadrilateral is named by its properties." clip: - caption: { text: "One pair of parallel sides (arrows): a trapezium.", say: "One pair of parallel sides: a trapezium." } - wait: 1400 - caption: { text: "Move A: now two pairs, and four right angles. A rectangle.", say: "Move one corner. Two pairs of parallel sides and four right angles: a rectangle." } - click: Move A left - expect: { selector: "#gclass", contains: "Rectangle" } - wait: 1000 - caption: { text: "It has every parallelogram property too.", say: "It has every property of a parallelogram too." } - wait: 1200 --- A **quadrilateral** has four sides. Its name comes from its **properties**: what is true about its sides and angles. ## Predict: square or rectangle? ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to whether a square is a rectangle surfaces the everyday meaning of 'rectangle' (longer than it is wide) against the property definition." check: type: predict q: "Is a square a rectangle?" options: ["Yes", "No: a rectangle has two long sides and two short sides", "Only a big square"] actual: "Yes. A rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles, and a square has four right angles. It is a special rectangle, with its sides equal too." ``` What does a shape need to be a rectangle? ## Run: a rectangle that is not a square ```step stage: run insight: "Dragging an irregular quadrilateral into a rectangle shows the properties appearing one by one (parallel arrows, right angles) and the board's 'also' names." try: { playground: board, starter: "shape.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Drag the corners to make a rectangle that is not a square. What else does the board say it is? Was your prediction right?", when: "z = 2", explain: "A rectangle is also a parallelogram. Make the sides equal as well and it becomes a square, which is also a rectangle." } ``` Watch for the arrows (parallel sides), ticks (equal sides) and right-angle marks. | Name | Properties | |---|---| | **trapezium** | at least one pair of parallel sides | | **parallelogram** | two pairs of parallel sides (opposite sides equal) | | **rhombus** | four equal sides (so two pairs of parallel sides) | | **rectangle** | four right angles (so two pairs of parallel sides) | | **square** | four equal sides and four right angles | | **kite** | two pairs of equal sides next to each other | The board marks **parallel** sides with matching arrows, **equal** sides with matching ticks, and right angles with a small square. When a shape has every property of another, it belongs to that family too: a square is also a rectangle, a rhombus and a parallelogram. ## Investigate: a family of properties ```step stage: investigate insight: "Each name is a list of properties, and having all of one name's properties puts a shape in that family; Sam lets an extra property exclude a square from the rectangles." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each quadrilateral to its defining property." pairs: - ["trapezium", "at least one pair of parallel sides"] - ["parallelogram", "two pairs of parallel sides"] - ["rhombus", "four equal sides"] - ["rectangle", "four right angles"] - ["kite", "two pairs of equal sides next to each other"] explain: "A square has four equal sides and four right angles, so it fits the rhombus, rectangle and parallelogram rows too." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#sam" text: "Sam decides whether a square is a rectangle. Click the line where his reasoning goes wrong." answer: 4 fault: logic misconception: square-not-rectangle explain: "Line 4: having an extra property (equal sides) does not take away the rectangle's properties. A square has four right angles, so it is a rectangle: a special one." - check: type: question q: "Which is always true?" options: ["Every rhombus is a parallelogram", "Every parallelogram is a rhombus", "Every rectangle is a square", "Every kite is a rhombus"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A parallelogram's sides need not all be equal.", "A rectangle's sides need not all be equal.", "A kite's opposite sides need not be equal."] explain: "A rhombus has two pairs of parallel sides, so it has the parallelogram's property: every rhombus is a parallelogram." ``` ### Properties first Here is how to name a quadrilateral: check the properties, from the most special. ```worked \text{4 equal sides, 4 right angles} \Rightarrow \text{square} :: Check the most special names first. \text{4 right angles} \Rightarrow \text{rectangle} :: Right angles but sides not all equal. \text{4 equal sides} \Rightarrow \text{rhombus} :: Equal sides but no right angles. \text{2 pairs parallel} \Rightarrow \text{parallelogram} :: Then parallelogram, trapezium (at least one pair), kite. ``` Now match each name to its property. ### Find the mistake Read Sam's reasoning. Does an extra property take a name away? ### Always true? ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time on the board: a rhombus that is not a square, a parallelogram that is neither, a kite, then the edge case of four equal sides with one right angle." try: { playground: board, starter: "shape.yml#free", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "shape.yml#free" hint: ["All four sides the same length, but no right angles.", "Try corners (1, 1), (6, 1), (9, 5) and (4, 5): each side is 5."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a rhombus that is not a square.", when: "z = 3", explain: "Four equal sides, no right angles. It is also a parallelogram and a kite." } - starter: "shape.yml#free" hint: "Two pairs of parallel sides, with no right angles and the sides not all equal." check: { type: board, text: "Make a parallelogram that is not a rectangle and not a rhombus.", when: "z = 4", explain: "For example (1, 1), (7, 1), (9, 5), (3, 5)." } - starter: "shape.yml#free" hint: ["Two short equal sides next to each other at the top, two long equal sides next to each other at the bottom.", "Try (5, 1), (8, 5), (5, 7), (2, 5)."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a kite that is not a rhombus.", when: "z = 6", explain: "Two pairs of equal sides next to each other, but not all four equal." } - check: type: question q: "Edge case: a quadrilateral has four equal sides and one right angle. What is it?" options: ["A square", "A rhombus that is not a square", "A kite", "It cannot exist"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Four equal sides make it a rhombus, and a rhombus's angles next to a right angle must be 90° too.", "It is a kite, but there is a more special name.", "It exists: think of a square."] explain: "A rhombus is a parallelogram, so angles next to each other add to 180° (co-interior). One right angle makes them all right angles: a square." ``` ### A rhombus Each task changes one thing. ### A plain parallelogram ### A kite ### One right angle ## Practise: naming quadrilaterals ```step stage: practise insight: "Naming from properties, a family question and an angle from parallel sides, mixed; a square excluded from the rectangles is the planted slip; the review keeps isosceles triangles fresh." tasks: - check: type: question q: "A quadrilateral has two pairs of parallel sides, no right angles, and sides that are not all equal. What is its most special name?" options: ["Parallelogram", "Rhombus", "Rectangle", "Trapezium"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Its sides are not all equal.", "It has no right angles.", "It is a trapezium too, but parallelogram is more special: two pairs of parallel sides."] explain: "Two pairs of parallel sides, nothing more: a parallelogram." - check: type: question q: "Which names fit a square?" options: ["Square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, trapezium and kite", "Only square", "Square and rectangle only", "Square and rhombus only"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A square has every property on the rectangle's and the rhombus's lists.", "It also has the rectangle's and the rhombus's properties.", "It has the rhombus's four equal sides too."] explain: "A square has all these properties, so it belongs to all these families." - check: type: answer q: "One angle of a parallelogram is 70°. What is the angle next to it, in degrees?" answer: "110" feedback: - ["70", "That is the opposite angle. Angles next to each other are co-interior."] - ["290", "Angles next to each other add to 180°, not 360°."] explain: "Neighbouring angles of a parallelogram are co-interior: 180 − 70 = 110°." - check: type: answer q: "Review: an isosceles triangle has two angles of 35°. What is the third, in degrees?" answer: "110" feedback: - ["145", "Both 35° angles count: 180 − 35 − 35."] explain: "180 − 35 − 35 = 110°." ``` ### Most special name ### All the names ### Angles in a parallelogram ### Review: triangles ## Make: a right-angled trapezium ```step stage: make insight: "Building a trapezium with a right angle that is not a parallelogram combines a parallel pair with a right angle while avoiding a second parallel pair." try: { playground: board, starter: "shape.yml#make", height: 600 } hint: ["Make the top and bottom parallel, then make one side straight up.", "Keep the other side slanted so there is only one parallel pair."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a trapezium that is not a parallelogram, with at least one right angle.", when: "z = 5 and g >= 1", explain: "For example (1, 1), (9, 1), (6, 5), (1, 5): one pair of parallel sides and two right angles." } ``` Then: how many right angles can such a trapezium have, and why not three? ## Make: names and a linkage, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A tray frame that is a rectangle when closed and a leaning parallelogram when open shows what each name promises, and why the tray stays level." hint: ["Which promises still hold when the frame leans: equal sides, parallel sides, right angles?", "What do parallel sides do to the tray?"] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A toolbox tray hangs from two arms of equal length that stay parallel. Closed, the four hinge points make a rectangle. As the tray swings open, the frame leans over. On paper, say which names still fit the leaning frame, and why the tray stays level." steps: - ["Closed: four right angles, so a rectangle (and a parallelogram)", "a rectangle is a special parallelogram"] - ["Leaning: both pairs of opposite sides are still parallel and equal, but the right angles are gone, so it is a parallelogram, not a rectangle", "a name stays only while all its properties hold"] - ["The tray bar is opposite the base bar, so it stays parallel to it: the tray stays level", "opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Which name still fits the leaning frame?" options: - "Parallelogram: opposite sides are still parallel and equal" - "Rectangle: it is the same frame, so it keeps its name" - "Neither: it is no longer a quadrilateral" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The right angles are gone, so it is no longer a rectangle.", "It still has four straight sides, so it is still a quadrilateral."] - step: 3 q: "Why does the tray stay level?" options: - "Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel, so the tray bar stays parallel to the base" - "The hinges are tight, so the tray cannot tip" - "The arms are long, so the tray hardly moves" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Friction might slow the tray, but it is not the reason it stays level.", "Even short arms keep it level. The shape is the reason."] criteria: - "I named the shape closed and open, using its properties." - "I said which property is lost when the frame leans." - "I linked parallel opposite sides to the tray staying level." explain: "Closed it is a rectangle, and also a parallelogram. Leaning, it keeps its parallel, equal opposite sides but loses its right angles, so it is a parallelogram only. Its opposite sides stay parallel, so the tray stays level." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The frame is made up for the task, but real toolbox trays swing like this. Write the names for the closed and the open frame, give the property for each, then choose the reasons that matter most. **Also used in** - **Desk lamps and barriers.** Parallelogram arms keep a lamp head or a barrier arm pointing the same way as it moves. - **Frames.** Calling a frame a rectangle promises right angles and equal diagonals, so a builder can check it by measuring. ```teacher summary: Students drag quadrilaterals until the board names them, learn the defining properties of the trapezium, parallelogram, rhombus, rectangle, square and kite, and reason about the family (a square is a rectangle and a rhombus) (AC9M7SP02, node 2). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can name a quadrilateral from its properties. - I can explain why a square is also a rectangle and a rhombus. - I can use parallel sides to find angles in a parallelogram. struggle: Accepting that one shape can have several names. Ask students to read a square's properties against each name's list, out loud, instead of telling them the answer. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need parallel lines and co-interior angles (Parallel lines unit). The one idea: a name is a list of properties, and a shape with every property on a list belongs to that family. This is the unit's hinge: students who hold the everyday meaning ("a rectangle is longer than wide") cannot reason about the family (Sam's mistake). Definitions: this site follows the Australian Curriculum glossary, where a trapezium has at least one pair of parallel sides, so every parallelogram (and rectangle, rhombus and square) is a trapezium too. Some textbooks say exactly one pair; mention it if yours does. running: - "Predict: take a vote; most say no. Keep the vote visible until after Investigate." - "Run: ask what the board added to its name as the rectangle appeared." - "Investigate: build a family tree on the board, from quadrilateral down to square." - "Modify: for the edge case, ask what co-interior angles say about the next corner." - "Make: ask why a trapezium can't have exactly three right angles." - "Paper: the linkage task is worked in books; the page marks two reasons (which name still fits, and why the tray stays level). Books out, then look at the page to compare the names for closed and open." stuck: - see: A student says a square is not a rectangle (Sam's mistake). ask: What does a shape need to be a rectangle? Does a square have it? fix: "Four right angles: yes. Extra properties don't remove a name." - see: A student names a rhombus a diamond and stops there. ask: What do its sides and its parallel pairs say? fix: "Four equal sides: rhombus (and so a parallelogram)." - see: A student cannot make a kite on the board. ask: "Which sides should be equal: opposite ones or neighbours?" fix: "Neighbours: two short ones together and two long ones together." stretch: Draw a Venn diagram of rectangles and rhombuses. What goes in the overlap? Where do parallelograms go? support: Use a property checklist (parallel pairs, equal sides, right angles) for every shape before naming it. leads: > Next: Polygons (node 3): regular or irregular, convex or concave. Where it leads: properties of diagonals and congruence proofs for quadrilaterals (Years 8 to 10). exit: q: A shape has two pairs of parallel sides and four equal sides but no right angles. Give all its names. a: Rhombus, parallelogram and kite. explain: > A quadrilateral's name comes from its **properties**: a **trapezium** has at least one pair of parallel sides; a **parallelogram** two; a **rhombus** four equal sides; a **rectangle** four right angles; a **square** four equal sides and four right angles; a **kite** two pairs of equal sides next to each other. A shape with all of another name's properties belongs to that family too: every square is a rectangle and a rhombus, every rhombus and rectangle is a parallelogram, and every parallelogram is a trapezium. ```

# Sam's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: sam
A square has four right angles.
A rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles.
A square also has two pairs of parallel sides, like a rectangle.
But a square is not a rectangle, because all its sides are equal.
# endregion
